newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly edge up with firmer gas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly edge up with firmer gas.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly edged higher Monday in lackluster trade, with surging East Coast city gate gas prices underpinning the complex despite propects for little utility demand, sources said.

"There aren't a lot of barrels available and (firmer) gas certainly isn't hurting. Resid should stay stable to firm," said one cash trader, noting forecasts for mild East Coast weather should keep utility burns low but surging gas prices should encourage some fuel switching to cheaper resid.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent gained 15 cents to $16.00-25 a barrel, with September one percent paper up a similar amount to $16.30-45 with firmer crude.

NYH 0.3 percent high pour was talked a quarter higher in the $18.25-50 range, still well supported by a New York utility's 850,000 barrel August buy program. Traders said 70,000 barrels of NYH August HP sold Friday at $18.40.
High sulphurs in New York climbed more than a quarter, with 2.2 percent now pegged at $15.25-50 or higher, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were stable, with three percent holding at $15.25 and one percent flat at about $16.

New York city gate gas prices jumped 20 cents Monday to the low-$2.70s/mmBtu, or $17.20 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed 15 cents to the low-$2.50s/mmBtu, or about $15.94 a barrel.
